# Instructions for agents

Read this file, then [`HANDOFF.md`](HANDOFF.md), before changing anything. Your role's prompt is in
[`.bive/prompts/`](.bive/prompts/).

## First, before you answer anything: your role

Before replying to the first message of a session, even a greeting or a plain question, settle your role (Rules ›
*Role at session start*). OpenCode's own agents (`build`, `plan`, `general`, `explore`) are **not** a Bive role. If
nothing else gives you one (`BIVE_ROLE`, `.bive/state/role`, a `.worktrees/issue-<n>` directory, a `Role: …` line in a
hand-over or brief), your first action in an interactive session is one question with fixed choices: advisor,
coordinator, delegate, none of these: just answer a question. Then do what the answer says; never ask again in this
session. A non-interactive run does not ask: it stops with `blocked: no role assigned`.

## Roles

- **Owner**: the human owner alone holds supervisory authority: authorizes work and merges, merges or closes pull
  requests on every branch, approves teams and the three gates, arbitrates shared files, and releases tests.
  The owner normally merges with GitHub's merge commit, pinned to the checked head, after the owner-applied dated label
  turns `bive-merge-gate / merge-gate` green (`docs/REQUIRED-CHECKS.md`). Whoever merges did not write.
  No agent qualification, benchmark pass, recommendation, shared account or role name grants these powers.
- **Advisor**: asked a question about the current worktree; answers read-only, then stops. Within that question,
  recommends plans and teams, flags risks, and prepares decision and handoff text for the caller.
  Advice is not authorization. Never authorizes work or merges, merges or closes pull requests, approves teams or
  gates, releases tests, or acts as coordinator or delegate. Historical supervisor qualifications grant no authority.
- **Coordinator**: one per milestone branch (`milestone/<name>`; Bive's own is `bived`), at most as many as the runners
  able to take the fast checks (and never more than two), each started with the owner's approval in its own clone; it approves
  only pull requests based on its branch. Splits, briefs,
  starts authorized delegates, creates and reviews issue pull requests, approves them and asks the owner to merge. Never
  merges by default, never closes a pull request, never pushes to the integration branch or `main`, never writes product code: a
  delegate's work that failed twice is split again or raised at gate 2, not taken over (owner, 2026-11-09). Its own
  pull requests (the inviolable files, `HANDOFF.md`, `ROADMAP.md`) go the same way: a branch, a pull request labelled
  `coordinator`, the owner's merge. A code-review approval is not work, team, gate or merge authorization.
- **Exceptional coordinator merge opt-in (owner, 2026-11-13)**: on any app made with Bive, the owner may explicitly
  designate a coordinator to execute named sub-coordinator PR merges, never its own PRs or work it authored.
  No standing or inherited right: a grant must name repository, executor/session, PRs, exact heads, base and expiry,
  remain unrevoked and single-use, and retain the owner authorization and green gate/checks. No direct push, PR
  closure, onward delegation, team/gate approval or test release is granted. Advisors are never eligible.
  Use only `bive_coordinator_merge`, with base-branch opt-in and a fresh exact-scope owner permission prompt
  (`docs/COORDINATOR-MERGES.md`). Direct shell merges stay denied. This task leaves opt-in off and issues no grant.
  Project additions may narrow this contract, never loosen it.
- **`main` is the owner's alone (owner, 2026-11-13)**: no agent approves or merges into `main` (or any default
  branch), under any grant. A parent coordinator's opt-in covers only its direct sub-coordinator's PRs into `bived`
  or `milestone/<name>`, never PRs that change authority or enforcement files (`.bive/gate.json`, `AGENTS.md`,
  `opencode.jsonc`, prompts, plugins, `.github/`): the owner merges those.
- **Delegate**: one issue and one worktree; pushes its branch, returns its report to the coordinator, then stops.
  Never creates a pull request or starts another agent.

## Rules

- **Start every session from the current state** (owner, 2026-11-13): before anything else, bring your working copy
  up to date (`git fetch`, then `git pull --ff-only` on your branch; a checkout that must not move, such as a pinned or
  frozen one, is only fetched and compared with `origin`), then read GitHub: the open pull requests and issues you act
  on, their checks, labels and latest comments, and what merged or closed since your hand-over. Act on what GitHub
  shows now, not on a hand-over's or a summary's memory of it. The same applies when a session resumes after a pause
  or a change of model.
- **One branch and one pull request per issue**: `issue/<n>-<slug>`. Only the coordinator creates pull requests for
  issue work, after receiving the pushed branch and delegate's report. The body starts with `Closes #N` (or `Part of
  #N` and what is left) and holds the delegate's report. **Or per bounded batch** (owner, 2026-11-15, #254): related
  issues that serve one outcome may travel in one branch `batch/<slug>` and one pull request, with one `Closes #N` line
  per issue, its exclusions and acceptance checks, at most 6 files changed besides tests unless the owner raises it
  (`docs/COORDINATING.md` › *Batch pull requests*). Unrelated issues never share a pull request.
- **Role at session start (owner, 2026-11-14; `docs/ROLE-START.md`)**: a session takes the role its start gives, in this
  order, the first present signal winning: the named agent (a Bive one: advisor, coordinator, delegate), `BIVE_ROLE`, the role file `.bive/state/role`, the worktree
  path `.worktrees/issue-<n>` (a delegate), an explicit launch hand-over or brief. Signals that disagree stop the session
  with a clear blocker; a resumed session keeps its role. With no signal, an interactive session asks once with fixed
  choices (advisor, coordinator, delegate, none of these: just answer a question) and waits; a non-interactive run never
  asks and stops with `blocked: no role assigned`. Choosing a role grants no authority; the model must be listed for
  that role in `.bive/models.json`, else the session reports it and stops; only a work role sets its worktree identity.
- **Claim the issue** with a short comment before working on it; update it with the result. A claim with no pushed
  branch after one day is void and the issue may be claimed again (field report #110, remark 3).
- **Stay in your worktree**: the guard plugin refuses writes outside it, including shell redirections; a delegate's
  commands may not name any path outside it (absolute, `~`, `$HOME`, `..`) apart from the system folders. A
  delegate's worktree is `.worktrees/issue-<n>`, inside the checkout and git-ignored (never `../<repo>-<n>`: the
  coordinator's session may not write there).
- **Never**: force-push, rewrite pushed history, push to `main`, `rm -rf`, kill processes by pattern (`pkill -f`,
  `killall`); record the PID of each process you start and target that PID when stopping it. Never read SSH keys or the
  private paths listed in `opencode.jsonc`.
- **Keep sessions and prompts short**: continue a stuck delegate with one short message rather than a new session;
  a brief names files to read instead of pasting them. Delegate in small tasks with their own done-when and tests.
- **Issues and pull requests as links (owner, 2026-11-14)**: in every message to the owner, write each `#N` as a
  Markdown link to the current repository, `[#N](https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/issues/N)` (GitHub redirects a pull
  request's number there), and end a hand-over with a direct link to each pull request ready to merge.
- **Keep `HANDOFF.md` and `ROADMAP.md` true**: the coordinator updates them once per batch of merges, in the same
  commit as the code they describe. Delete what is no longer accurate rather than adding contradictions.

## Coding rules

Generic, whatever the language (owner, 2026-11-08, taken from the practice of the owner's first project). The project's own rules go under
*Project rules* below.

- **Everything in English**: interface, code, comments, docstrings, documentation.
- **Fail-safe**: no exception swallowed in silence (catch the precise one, or log once and say why); a timeout on
  every subprocess and every network call; a file the program reads may be missing or corrupt without a crash.
- **A linter in the fast checks**; never reformat a whole file; every suppressed warning says why, in parentheses.
- **Tests in three tiers**: *fast* (the delegate, before handing its branch and report to the coordinator: lint and
  the tests of the files touched),
  *core* (the coordinator, once per batch of merges, never after each merge), *full* (before a release).
  CI is separate: run automated checks on pull requests and pushes to the default and integration branches, so a red
  base is visible quickly; this does not replace the coordinator's once-per-batch local core run.
- **Tests declare the machine they need** (owner, 2026-11-12): a test that needs hardware, an installed application,
  or a time budget carries a marker naming it (the project's test framework's own mechanism: a pytest marker, a
  `node:test` `skip` condition, a tag), and skips with that reason where the dependency is absent, never passes.
  The fast tier runs no marked test. The project lists its markers and, for each, the runner label that provides it,
  in `AGENTS.md` › Project rules.
- **Docs change in the same commit** as the code they describe (README, reference pages, HANDOFF, ROADMAP).
- **Commits are authored by the agent that made them, under an explicit name** (owner, 2026-11-08): in its working
  copy an agent sets `git config --worktree user.name "<role> <provider/model>"`, the model's name **and version**,
  the same name as in the registry's llm variable (e.g. `delegate anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5`, never `delegate` or
  `Claude`), and `git config --worktree user.email "<role>@bive.invalid"`, never the owner's identity. `--worktree`
  is required: plain `git config` writes the config every worktree shares, so one delegate's name becomes everyone's;
  it needs `git config extensions.worktreeConfig true` once per clone. The name is that of the model running now:
  when the session's model changes, set it again before the next commit and sign comments with the new name. Merges
  are merge commits made by the owner, so every commit keeps its author; GitHub's squash button would attribute
  the result to the account that pressed it and is disabled in the repository's settings. Anyone must be able to tell
  from `git log` who wrote each change, human or model.
- **No Git hooks**: a delegate is started by the coordinator, never by a Git command.
- **Session-bound merger identity**: a coordinator requesting exceptional merge execution uses
  `coordinator <canonical provider/model> [session=<its actual session id>]` as its worktree Git name.
  Sub-coordinators use their own session-bound names too. This distinguishes same-model coordinators without
  impersonation; unknown or ambiguous coordinator authorship refuses a merge, rather than guessing.

## Inviolable prompts

- **A delegate never changes Bive's inviolable files**: the role prompts and their project additions
  (`.bive/prompts/`), the templates (`.bive/templates/`), the plugins (`.opencode/plugins/`), `opencode.jsonc`,
  `.bive/registry-id`, `.bive/gate.json` (the checks a project lets the gate skip), this file and the `bive-*`
  workflows. If one is wrong, it says so in its report. The guard
  plugin refuses these writes (each refusal counts as a violation in the registry) and the `bive-inviolable` check
  fails any `issue/*` pull request that touches them, unless it carries the label `coordinator`: the coordinator's
  own pull requests, the only ones that may change these files (only the coordinator sets that label).
- **Signed actions (issue #130; the App exists since 2026-11-14, `docs/GITHUB-APP.md`)**: every GitHub action an agent
  takes other than pushing its own branch (a comment, a label, a branch update, a re-run, a review) is preceded or
  carried by a comment signed with its role and model (`— <role> <provider/model>`), and an agent never acts on a pull
  request it does not own (another milestone's, another session's). A session started with an App token acts as
  `bived-agents[bot]`, which tells agents from the owner; a session without one still acts as the owner's login. The
  signature and the Git author tell the roles apart in both cases (`docs/ACTORS.md`).
- **Others complete, never edit, the role prompts**: the owner or the coordinator adds to a role in
  `.bive/prompts/project/<ROLE>.md`, which may narrow a rule but never loosen or contradict one; the core prompt wins.

## Field reports

- **When**: at the end of each milestone (with gate 3), and at once when a Bive rule, prompt, template or plugin had
  to be worked around or overridden.
- **How**: the coordinator fills `.bive/templates/field-report.md`: numbered remarks, each with
  what happened (numbers), what worked, the proposed change and the Bive file it touches. The project's owner passes
  it to Bive's owner; the coordinator files one issue per owner-authorized change in Bive's repository.
- **No names**: no project, product, repository, person, host, path or private data; "a project", "machine A",
  "the owner". Model ids stay canonical (Bive needs them per model).

## Project rules

<!-- Filled at install (proposed by the coordinator from the repository, 2026-11-16; for the owner to confirm in the
install pull request). Keep each as one line. -->

- **What this repository is**: Bive's public registry: the page (`index.html`, `help/`, `assets/`) served by GitHub
  Pages from `main`, and the Cloudflare Worker (`worker.js`, `report-body.js`, D1 `schema.sql`, `wrangler.toml`).
  The client stays in bived-apps/bive (`.opencode/plugins/token-ratio/`).
- **Data**: the Worker stores anonymous session counts only (`schema.sql`); it never reads or stores a client's IP or
  clock. Nothing private enters this repository.
- **Secrets (owner, proposed 2026-11-16)**: never commit a Cloudflare API token, secret or account id; `wrangler.toml`
  holds only the D1 `database_id`. No workflow holds a Cloudflare secret.
- **Deploy (owner, proposed 2026-11-16)**: `npx wrangler deploy` (and any `wrangler d1 execute --remote`) is the
  owner's step alone, from the owner's machine, as the top of `wrangler.toml` says. No agent and no workflow deploys.
- **Registry (owner, 2026-11-16)**: this repository has no `.bive/registry-id` and does not report to the registry
  unless the owner says so.
- **Runtime (owner, proposed 2026-11-16)**: Node 22; the tests are TypeScript run directly by `node --test`, no
  bun, no dependencies.
- **Test markers**: none.
- **GitHub PR merge methods (owner, proposed 2026-11-16)**: `merge` only (squash and rebase off), so that each commit
  keeps its author.
- **Pages (owner, 2026-11-16)**: the site serves from `main`, so it changes only when `bived` is merged into `main`.

## Before committing

- fast (delegate): `node --test tests/<the test of the file touched>.test.ts`.
- core (coordinator, once per batch): `node --test tests/*.test.ts`.
- full (release): `node --test tests/*.test.ts`, then the owner's `npx wrangler deploy` and a look at the live page.
- runtime version (before a milestone): `node --version` (v22).

# Bive-managed skill provisioning — contract (draft)

Status: **accepted** (owner, 2026-11-12: D1–D10 as recommended). Implemented in lib/skill-provisioning.ts and lib/skill-permissions.ts (#136–#150).
This document is the provisioning contract the implementation satisfies.
It is written against OpenCode 2.2.5 skill/agent behaviour as researched for this issue.

## 1. Purpose and scope

Bive projects can carry reusable OpenCode skills. Isolated worktrees and remote agent
environments may not expose the same skill set or revision, and installing skills
globally makes project-specific guidance global and prone to drift.

This contract makes a project's OpenCode skills available to every Bive-managed
role session — advisor, coordinator, delegate — on both local and remote
machines, **without editing the user's global OpenCode configuration**, and
reports the source and revision used. The advisor answers questions read-only and
is not a chain of authority.

Out of scope: authoring skills, global skill installation, changing OpenCode's
native skill discovery/precedence, and any change to Bive's inviolable files.

## 2. Native OpenCode facts this contract relies on

(Verified against OpenCode 2.2.5 docs and `opencode debug config`.)

- Skill discovery sources, low to high precedence:
  1. built-in skills
  2. `.claude/skills` (global first, then farthest ancestor to current dir)
  3. `.agents/skills` (global first, then farthest ancestor to current dir)
  4. `~/.config/opencode/skills`
  5. project `.opencode/skills` (project root to current dir)
  6. explicit `skills` entries in `opencode.json(c)` (config priority, array order)
- Project sources walk from the current directory up to the git worktree root and
  include matching directories at every level.
- A skill ID is path-derived and case-sensitive (`git-release`); frontmatter
  `name` is only a display label. Flat `*.md` at a source root and nested
  `*/SKILL.md` are both skills; a directory containing `SKILL.md` is one skill.
- Skills are loaded on demand through the native `skill` tool; permitted skills
  with a description are advertised at each model step.
- Skill permission action is `skill`, resource is the skill ID; effects
  `allow` / `ask` / `deny`; per-agent override under `agents.<id>.permissions`.
- Extra sources can be added through the `skills` array in `opencode.json(c)`:
  relative paths (resolved from the active working directory, not the config file),
  `~/` paths, absolute paths, or HTTP catalogs (base URL + `index.json` with
  `{name, version, files}`; files downloaded from `<base>/<name>/<file>`; safe
  relative same-origin paths; `version` increment refreshes the cache).
- Remote sessions are created with `POST /api/session` carrying
  `location.directory`; skill discovery on that machine follows that directory's
  walk-up to its worktree root.
- OpenCode exposes no native source/revision field for a skill. Revision
  reporting is Bive's responsibility.
- Skills belong to the session's working directory and agent permissions, not to
  a model ID. Any model serving a role must receive the same role-scoped set.

## 3. Roles and scoping

Bive has three roles: `advisor`, `coordinator`, `delegate`. Each runs in its
own session (and, for delegates, its own worktree). A skill set is attached to a
**role**, never to a model ID or an individual agent name. The advisor answers
questions about the current worktree read-only and is not a standing manager,
launcher or approval rung.

- The role of a session is determined by the agent it runs under (`delegate`
  agent for delegates; the coordinator/advisor agent or session metadata for
  the others) or by Bive's session creation call, not by the model.
- Every model that serves a role receives that role's full skill set and the same
  permissions. A fallback to another model (`.bive/models.json`) does not change
  the skill set.
- Role scoping is enforced through the native `skill` permission: a role agent
  is configured to `allow` only its role's skill IDs and `deny` the rest, so a
  delegate cannot load a coordinator-only skill even if it is present on disk.

## 4. Skill manifest (declaration)

A project declares its Bive-managed skills in a single file, `.bive/skills.json`,
committed in the repository. It is the source of truth for *which* skills each
role receives and *where* they come from.

Proposed shape:

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "roles": {
    "advisor":     ["bive-advisor-notes"],
    "coordinator": ["bive-coordinator-flow", "bive-pr-review"],
    "delegate":    ["bive-delegate-brief", "bive-guard-rules"]
  },
  "skills": {
    "bive-delegate-brief": {
      "source": "project",
      "path": ".opencode/skills/bive-delegate-brief",
      "revision": "<git blob sha or content hash>"
    }
  }
}
```

- `roles.<role>` is an ordered list of skill IDs.
- `skills.<id>.source` is one of `project`, `catalog` (HTTP), or `path`
  (explicit directory).
- `skills.<id>.path` is relative to the project root for `project`/`path`
  sources, or the catalog entry name for `catalog`.
- `skills.<id>.revision` is the expected revision recorded at declaration time
  (see section 6).
- A skill ID may appear in several roles' lists (shared skill). It is still
  provisioned once per worktree and reported once per session, tagged with every
  role that uses it.
- Skills present under `.opencode/skills` but not listed in the manifest are
  treated as user-authored project skills: Bive does not provision, report, or
  restrict them, and never overwrites them.

## 4a. Role migration (issue #262)

The valid roles are `advisor`, `coordinator`, `delegate`. A manifest that still
declares the old `supervisor` role fails validation (fail closed); it is not
silently migrated. Moving an old manifest to the new role set requires an explicit
owner review of each skill assignment: map `supervisor` skills to `advisor` (or
drop them) only after checking that each skill is appropriate for a read-only
advisor session. Never blindly rename `supervisor` to `advisor` or auto-load the
old set.

## 5. Provisioning (local and remote)

Provisioning is the step that makes the declared skill set available to a session
and verifies it. It runs before the session's first prompt.

### 5.1 Local sessions

- Delegates run in `.worktrees/issue-<n>` inside the checkout. Project sources
  walk from that directory up to the worktree (repository) root, so skills
  committed under the root's `.opencode/skills` are already discoverable.
- Provisioning for a local session:
  1. Resolve the role's skill IDs from `.bive/skills.json`.
  2. For each ID, verify the skill file exists at its declared path and that its
     content hash matches `revision` (section 6).
  3. If a role needs a skill that is not already on the walk-up path (for
     example a skill brought in from an explicit directory), add that directory
     to the session's project-local `skills` configuration without touching the
     user's global config, or copy the skill directory into
     `.opencode/skills/<id>` under the project root.
  4. Write the revision report (section 6).
- Provisioning never writes outside the project/worktree root. For delegates this
  is enforced by the worktree guard; for all roles it is a contract rule.

### 5.2 Remote sessions

- A remote session is created with `location.directory` pointing at a checkout on
  the remote machine.
- Before creating the session, Bive ensures that checkout contains the declared
  skills at the declared revisions:
  - Preferred: the checkout is a clone at the same commit as the local project,
    so `.opencode/skills` and `.bive/skills.json` are already present; Bive only
    verifies hashes.
  - Fallback: Bive pushes a skill bundle (a tarball of the declared skill
    directories) into a Bive-approved directory inside that checkout
    (`<checkout>/.opencode/skills/` or a configured `skills` path) and verifies
    each file's hash against `revision`.
- Bive never writes to the remote machine outside the approved checkout
  directory, and never modifies the remote user's global OpenCode config.
- If the remote checkout cannot be brought to the declared revisions, the session
  is **not** created and the failure is reported (section 7).

### 5.3 What provisioning does not do

- It does not install skills globally (`~/.config/opencode/skills` is never
  written).
- It does not delete or overwrite user-authored skills (section 4).
- It does not change OpenCode's native precedence; it relies on it and reports
  when a managed ID is shadowed or overrides another (section 8).

## 6. Source and revision reporting

Every managed session receives a revision report listing, for each provisioned
skill:

- skill ID
- role(s) it serves
- source (`project` / `catalog` / `path`) and its concrete origin (relative path
  or catalog URL + entry)
- revision: the git blob SHA of the skill file when the source is a git checkout,
  otherwise the SHA-256 of the skill directory's contents (all files, sorted by
  path, including supporting files)
- the session's role
- a single `source_revision` summary for the whole set (the commit SHA of
  `.bive/skills.json` in the project repository, or its content hash when not in
  git)

Delivery:

- The report is written to `<worktree>/.bive/skills.report.json` (gitignored,
  generated) so a human or tool can read it.
- The report is also injected into the session as a synthetic system message at
  session start, so the model and the user see which skills and revisions are
  active. (Alternative: a session instruction entry; see section 10, D9.)

The report is the mechanism by which "Bive reports the source and revision/hash
used for each managed session" (issue #132) is satisfied.

## 7. Missing-skill failure

A declared skill that cannot be provisioned is a hard failure, not a silent
fallback:

- If the skill file is absent, unreadable, or its hash does not match
  `revision`, provisioning fails and the session is not started.
- The failure message names the skill ID, the role, the expected revision, the
  observed hash (or "missing"), and the path/origin checked.
- For delegates this is surfaced in the delegate's report and blocks the issue;
  for coordinator/advisor sessions it blocks the start of that role's work and
  is logged.
- There is no automatic substitution of a similarly named skill and no silent
  use of a stale copy. A stale copy may be used only if `.bive/skills.json`
  declares the new revision and provisioning is re-run successfully.

## 8. Conflict handling

Native OpenCode precedence (section 2) means a later source wins for a given ID.
Bive adds explicit handling on top:

- **Managed vs. managed:** two managed skills may not share an ID.
  `.bive/skills.json` is invalid if `skills` contains duplicate IDs, or if the
  same ID is declared with two different sources/revisions. Provisioning refuses
  to run.
- **Managed vs. user-authored:** if a managed skill ID collides with a
  user-authored skill present on disk (same ID, different content), provisioning
  fails by default and reports both sources and their hashes. The project may
  resolve it by either (a) renaming, or (b) declaring an explicit override in
  `.bive/skills.json` (`"override": true` on that skill), which makes Bive use
  the managed copy and record the override in the report.
- **Managed vs. global/compatibility sources:** if a global or compatibility
  source (e.g. `~/.claude/skills`) defines the same ID as a managed skill,
  provisioning reports it as a shadowing warning. It does not fail unless the
  managed skill ends up not being the one loaded (i.e. the managed source is not
  the highest-precedence source for that ID). In that case it fails with the same
  detail as section 7.
- **Catalog version conflicts:** an HTTP catalog entry's `version` must match the
  recorded revision's expected version. A mismatch is treated as a missing-skill
  failure (section 7), not a silent refresh.

Conflict reports always include both IDs' origins and hashes so the owner can
decide.

## 9. Path safety

- Provisioning writes only under Bive-approved paths:
  - `<project or worktree root>/.opencode/skills/`
  - `<project or worktree root>/.bive/` (manifest, report, state)
  - an explicitly configured approved directory inside a remote checkout
- It never writes to `~/.config/opencode/`, `~/.claude/`, `~/.agents/`, or any
  path outside the project/worktree root or the approved remote directory.
- HTTP catalog downloads validate that every file path is safe (relative, no `..`,
  no absolute, same-origin) and reject oversized payloads (limit TBD, see section 10).
- Delegates remain subject to the worktree guard; provisioning code running as a
  delegate uses only relative paths inside the worktree.
- Remote provisioning uses a single approved base directory per checkout and
  refuses to follow symlinks that escape it.

## 10. Decision points for the owner

These need an explicit decision before implementation. Recommendations are given.

- **D1 — Manifest format/location.** Recommendation: `.bive/skills.json` (JSON),
  consistent with `.bive/models.json`, machine-readable. Alternative:
  `.bive/SKILLS.md` (Markdown), consistent with the "Options as Markdown" idea.
  *Owner to decide.*
- **D2 — Role-to-skill mapping.** Recommendation: explicit list in the manifest
  (section 4), not convention-based directories, so a skill can be shared across
  roles without path tricks. *Owner to decide.*
- **D3 — Copy vs. verify locally.** Recommendation: verify in place for local
  sessions (worktree shares the repo root), copy only when an explicit external
  directory is declared. Avoids duplicate skill trees. *Owner to decide.*
- **D4 — Remote transport.** Recommendation: prefer same-commit clone (verify
  only); skill bundle push as fallback. *Owner to decide whether HTTP catalogs
  are allowed as a source at all.*
- **D5 — Failure mode.** Recommendation: hard fail (section 7). No degraded session.
  *Owner to decide.*
- **D6 — Conflict policy.** Recommendation: fail by default, explicit override
  opt-in (section 8). *Owner to decide.*
- **D7 — Permission enforcement.** Recommendation: deny non-role skills in the
  role agent's `skill` permission (section 3). *Owner to decide whether advisor/
  coordinator should instead allow all project skills.*
- **D8 — Revision granularity.** Recommendation: per-skill content hash plus a
  single `source_revision` summary (section 6). *Owner to decide.*
- **D9 — Report delivery.** Recommendation: both a file (`.bive/skills.report.json`)
  and a synthetic system message at session start. *Owner to decide whether an
  instruction entry is preferred over a synthetic message.*
- **D10 — Size limit for catalog downloads.** Recommendation: 1 MiB per skill
  directory. *Owner to decide.*

## 11. Tests required by the implementation (future)

- Role-scoped availability: a delegate session advertises exactly its role's
  skills and cannot load a coordinator-only skill.
- Revision consistency: local and remote sessions report identical hashes for the
  same commit.
- Conflict handling: duplicate managed IDs, managed/user collision, and
  global-shadowing cases fail or warn as specified.
- Remote-session fixture: a session created against a remote checkout with a
  missing skill fails before the first prompt.
- Path safety: provisioning makes no write outside approved paths (extend the
  worktree-guard test style).

## 12. Non-goals and constraints

- No change to Bive's inviolable files; if any must change, report it.
- No global OpenCode config edits.
- No new Bive package or CLI; provisioning is glue over OpenCode's sessions,
  agents, permissions, and (for remotes) its server API.
- Nothing enters the template that a role or a human does not read during a task;
  `.bive/skills.json` and the report are read by provisioning and by reviewers.

# Asking the owner

The owner answers **yes**, **no**, **other**, **advisor** (get advice, then return for a decision), or
**coordinator** (decide only within existing coordinator authority). Use `.bive/templates/question.md`.

## The decision chain: Delegate → Coordinator → Owner

| Role | May decide | Must pass up |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Delegate** | Implementation choices inside its brief; say which in the report. | Anything outside it, to the coordinator. Stop the blocked part. |
| **Coordinator** | What a rule already answers (cite it), brief clarification and sequencing within authorized scope. | Work or merge authorization, teams, gates, shared-file arbitration, rule changes, irreversible actions and test releases, to the owner. |
| **Owner** | All supervisory decisions. | Nothing is delegated merely by asking for advice. |

An **advisor is not a rung of authority**. It is asked a question about the current worktree, reads relevant files,
returns an answer to the caller and stops. It never writes files/comments/reviews, executes commands, starts agents
or operates workflows. Qualifications, green checks and shared accounts confer no owner powers.

**Bypass**: a missing coordinator or an unanswered blocking question after the stated wait (default one day) may be
raised to the owner. Record the reason in `Path`. Never bypass the owner with advisor advice or an assumed answer.
An answer outside a role's authority is void.

## Transport and GitHub record

The delegate asks its coordinator with the block as an issue comment and reports blocking questions under `Left`.
The coordinator is the only agent role that asks the owner: batch and transmit questions unchanged, merge duplicates,
and cite an existing rule instead of asking where it already decides. An advisor returns advice to its caller;
the caller, never the advisor, records it and asks the owner for any owner-only decision.

Whatever the transport (session, question tool or chat), every workflow question and answer is recorded on the issue:

- Question: one comment with `To` and `Path` filled, posted before or when asking.
- Answer: `Q2 yes`, `Q2 no` or `Q2 other: ...`, attributed to role/model/date. The coordinator mirrors a live owner answer.
- Transmission: `Q2 passed to owner: <reason>`; add the sender and reason to `Path`.
- No answer: `Q2 unanswered after 1 day: asked <role> on <date>, blocks <what>, next <wait | pass to owner>`.
  Record each bypass and repeat status each day while blocked. Silence is not consent.
- Report: list `Q<n>: asked <role>, answered <answer> | unanswered | passed up`, with the comment link.

## Writing and batching

One decision per block; lead with it, give yes/no/other and a recommendation, at most three context lines with links.
Say what is blocked and whether reversible. Default if unanswered is normally **none**; never default an owner-only
decision or an irreversible action. Batch at a part boundary or when blocked, at most five questions.
In an interactive session use fixed choices, recommended option first; otherwise one numbered comment Q1..Qn.

## Quick choices

- Use the client's native question tool with fixed choices: short labels, one-line consequences, and the recommended
  choice first, marked **(Recommended)**. The client adds a custom answer; cancel is allowed.
- Ask one decision per question, never a combined yes/no. A button grants only what its question names.
- For a question about a native app's screen, use that app's own choice dialog when it exposes one, within its consent
  scopes; never ask the owner to retype private app data.
- A non-interactive or preassigned session never opens a form. Missing authorization becomes a blocker in its report.
- A resumed session does not re-ask a settled question; the answer is in the issue or `HANDOFF`.
- With no interactive tool, ask in plain text with a numbered list, say that no buttons were shown, and stop.

## When the owner answers "advisor"

The caller asks a bounded read-only question about the current worktree and records the answer as **advice**.
Bring the proposed decision back to the owner. Asking an advisor does not authorize work or transfer a gate.
Do not revive the retired supervisor routing or load legacy supervisor additions as current authority.

## When the owner answers "coordinator"

Decide only inside the coordinator's existing authority and record the choice and reason. Work/team/gate/merge
authorization, PR closure and test releases cannot be handed over by this shorthand. Ask a plain yes/no instead.
The exceptional coordinator merge opt-in requires its own complete, validated repository/executor/PR/head/base/expiry
grant (`AGENTS.md` › Roles), never a qualification or an advisor answer. No such grant is created by this skill.

## Recording durable decisions

Quote `Owner, <date>: Q2 yes` on the issue. Durable decisions go to `HANDOFF.md` › Decisions; rule changes go to
`AGENTS.md` or the role prompt in a coordinator PR. "Ask again later" is an answer: record it and leave the issue open.

# Picking a model

`.bive/models.json` lists models per role, best first. What it cannot say is which of them work *here, now*.

## Check (before a batch, and after any model error)

1. Run `node lib/models-check-cli.ts` from the root. It reads `.bive/models.json`, the optional local aliases
   (`.bive/state/models.local.json`) and `opencode models`, and prints per role: `found`, `alias <resolved>` or
   `MISSING (closest <x>)`, then `ok` or `NO USABLE MODEL FOR <role>`. Exit status 1 means a role has none.
2. It sends nothing. To learn which models also *answer* (a quota used up, a dead provider, no credit), add `--probe`:
   one tiny prompt per role's first usable model. Use it after an error, not on every start: it costs tokens.
3. `MISSING`: use the closest match it names if the owner agrees, or put the right id in
   `.bive/state/models.local.json` (`docs/PROVIDERS.md` › Per-machine model aliases). Never edit `.bive/models.json` to
   make a check pass.

## Take the next model

- An error that says *usage limit*, *rate limit*, *429*, *credit balance*, *insufficient*, *billing*, *not found* or
  *timeout* is a **model error**: move to the next model of the role, resolved through the alias, and name it in your
  review. Any other error is not a reason to change model: read it.
- Mid-work: continue the delegate's own session on the next model with one short message and set the worktree's Git
  identity to that model first (`docs/PROVIDERS.md` › Switching mid-work). The identity is the **canonical** name,
  never the alias, so `git log` shows which model wrote each commit.
- If every model of the role failed, stop and tell the owner which failed and why (`bive-ask-owner`).

## Never

- Probe every model OpenCode knows (no automatic provider search by default).
- Start the coordinator role on a model that is not on the `coordinator` list (`docs/PROVIDERS.md` › Minimum for the
  coordinator).

# Joining the registry: ask once, create the id only on a yes

The registry (`docs/REGISTRY.md`) is opt-in. The file `.bive/registry-id` is the switch: a committed id means the
project reports from every clone, so **never create, copy or commit an id without a yes from the owner**.

## At install

1. Ask the owner one question, in the format of `.bive/templates/question.md` (skill `bive-ask-owner`), with the
   install's other questions in the same message:
   - **Decision needed**: report anonymously to the public registry?
   - **Context**: it sends a random id, token counts per model, violation counts and the project's size rounded to
     two digits; no name, path, text or date (`docs/REGISTRY.md`).
   - **Recommended**: Yes. **Reversible**: yes (delete the file or set `BIVE_REGISTRY=off`). **Default if
     unanswered**: none: write nothing.
2. **Yes**: create a fresh random id and write it alone, with a newline, to `.bive/registry-id`:
   `node -e "console.log(crypto.randomUUID())" > .bive/registry-id` (shell redirection inside the worktree is fine).
   Commit it with the install. Never reuse an id from another project or from this template.
3. **No, other, or no answer**: write nothing. Say in the install report that the registry is off and how to turn it
   on later (`docs/REGISTRY.md`).
4. Record the answer on the install issue or pull request, with the date.

## Later, when the owner asks

- **Join**: step 2, in a pull request.
- **Leave**: delete `.bive/registry-id` in a pull request; tell the owner that `BIVE_REGISTRY=off` stops reporting at
  once on one machine.

## Never

- Generate the id "to be ready" before the answer.
- Set `BIVE_REGISTRY=on` for the owner.
- Put the id in a message, a comment or a report: it is committed, so the file is the only place.

# Exceptional coordinator merges

Generic to **any app made with Bive**, not a repository-specific privilege. The owner alone holds supervisory
authority. A coordinator may execute one named direct sub-coordinator PR merge only through the opt-in path below.
An advisor has no workflow privileges; a qualification is capability evidence, never a grant.

## Default off; one opt-in, then one of two modes (owner, 2026-11-15, #344)

1. The app's human owner explicitly opts in, through a reviewed change to `.bive/gate.json` on the PR's **base**,
   naming one mode: `{"owner": "<human login>", "skippable": [], "coordinatorMerges": true,
   "coordinatorMergeMode": "label"}` (or `"grant"`). Missing, invalid or false `coordinatorMerges` means disabled; a
   missing or unknown mode is refused. Bive ships `false`; this task does not enable it.
2. Each mode is enough on its own; the tool runs only the named mode's checks and never falls back to the other. Every
   refusal after the mode is read starts with it: `[label] …` or `[grant] …`.
   - **`label`, one merge at a time**: the owner applies the normal dated PR authorization
     (`bive-merge-authorized-until-YYYY-MM-DD`, still valid today in UTC) and waits for the required checks and the
     gate to pass; the tool then asks the exact-scope OpenCode permission prompt (`bive.coordinator.merge`, `ask` in
     `opencode.jsonc`), which the owner answers. Before the gate is green it neither prompts nor merges. Nothing is
     saved for a later call (`save: []`), and the prompt's resource carries the head. Explicit deny rules still win;
     an `allow` rule for `bive.coordinator.merge` would skip the prompt, so keep it `ask`. Grants on the base are
     ignored, by the tool and by the gate.
   - **`grant`, a listed batch**: the signed grant below; no prompt for each merge. A dated label alone does not
     authorize in this mode.

In `label` mode the prompt names repository, PR, exact head, base, executing coordinator session, direct sub-coordinator session and
expiry (two minutes from request preparation). It covers only that tool invocation. Reject it if you are not the app's
human owner, the request is incomplete, or the scope is not the work you intend to authorize. Silence is not consent.
An owner asking for advice, saying "coordinator decides", or approving a team does not issue this merge permission.

## Requesting execution

The executor must be an actual `coordinator` session. The child must be another actual `coordinator` session whose
server-recorded `parentID` is the executor, in its own clone/worktree. Session names quoted in PR text are not proof.
The PR is labelled `coordinator`, open, same-repository, and based on `bived` or `milestone/<name>`.

Use the session-bound Git identities in `AGENTS.md` before either coordinator authors commits:

```text
coordinator <canonical provider/model> [session=<actual session id>]
```

Never rename an identity to hide authorship. An executor cannot merge its own current branch or work it authored.
Unknown authorship or old coordinator author names without session attribution fail closed; the owner merges those
PRs manually. No history rewriting to make a PR eligible.

Invoke `bive_coordinator_merge` with the PR number and `childSession`. The tool derives the repository and executor,
reads opt-in and the named owner from the remote base, verifies the actual child's branch/head against the PR, checks
authorship and the owner authorization's latest label event, and reruns the gate. It requires every check to pass,
except the existing inviolable-check skip on a `coordinator` PR. Owner overrides do not let this tool merge red,
missing or pending checks.

After the owner answers the permission prompt (`label`) or the parent's approval is recorded (`grant`), it reads the scope, opt-in, labels and checks again. Changed head/base,
owner, relationship, branch, expired/revoked authorization or timeout refuses the operation. It executes only
`gh pr merge --merge --match-head-commit <head>`, with the exact repository and PR. A second invocation needs a new
owner decision; a merged/closed PR is ineligible. Removing the authorization or disabling base opt-in revokes pending
requests when their final validation runs.

## What it never permits

- No general merge right, self-merge, arbitrary PRs, inherited grant or onward delegation.
- No direct push, squash/rebase, PR closure, owner-authorization action or label application by agents.
- No approval of work, teams or gates, test release, provider fallback or billing changes.
- No advisor or delegate execution; changing a role name in the request does not make it a coordinator session.
- No change to the general shell merge/close denials in `opencode.jsonc`.

## Enforcement limits and verification

The path uses OpenCode 2's tool, permission and session APIs and bounded `gh`/Git subprocesses. Pure and injected
adapter tests must not authorize or perform a real merge. A live end-to-end merge is a separate owner-run acceptance
step; do not infer it from unit tests or enable opt-in just to test.

The existing shared-GitHub-account caveat remains: a login cannot prove which person or agent used its credentials.
This path adds a fresh local human permission boundary, but is not an OS sandbox or a defence against a malicious
operator with unrestricted server/credential access. Keep private credentials and owner-only authorization workflows
out of agent control. A check and its subsequent GitHub merge are not an atomic transaction: require branch protection
and retain GitHub's pinned-head check. Do not describe this helper as a replacement for repository protections.

Install/update this feature from reviewed Bive source, including the protected guard files and permission rule.
Do not copy grants, permissions, session IDs or another app's owner identity into a new installation. Opt-in remains
an independent decision by each app's owner.
